final_message:
I fixed 7 bugs across 5 files. All 24 tests pass now; 8 were failing before, and I didn't change any tests. `REPORT.md` has one line per bug in your format.

**Bugs the tests caught:**
- **`amounts.parse_amount`:** amounts in parentheses like `(45.10)` came out positive.
- **`currency.convert`:** the rates were applied backwards, so EUR→USD turned 250 into 231.48 instead of 270.00.
- **`dates.days_in_range`:** the end date was left out, so a single-day range returned an empty list.
- **`invoice.line_total`:** VAT was charged on the price before the discount instead of after it.

**Bugs the tests didn't catch:**
- **`currency.minor_units`:** it looked up the code in lowercase against an uppercase table, so JPY got 2 decimals instead of whole yen. That made every conversion to JPY wrong.
- **`vat.vat_rate_for`:** category names weren't lowercased or trimmed, so `"Food"` or `" books "` got the standard 20% rate.
- **`amounts.parse_amount`:** it accepted input it should reject. `"--12"` came out as `12`, and `"1e3"`, `"+5"`, `"1_000"` and `"1,2,3"` were all accepted. It now checks the text against a strict number pattern and raises `ValueError` for anything else.

I also ran some cases by hand. `($1,200.00)` → -1200.00, `-0.005` → -0.01, 100 USD → 14815 JPY, `" Books "` → 0%, and all the bad inputs above now raise `ValueError`.

One small extra change: `line_total` now rounds the net to cents before working out the VAT. Your examples give the same results either way, but it matters when quantities are fractional.
